findings.title: Upsampling gate matches the raw request query, so negated and split-path queries get `sum(sample_weight)`
findings.description:
`_is_error_focused_query` uses a substring test for `event.type:error`. That string also appears in the negation `!event.type:error`, so a discover query that excludes errors passes the gate. Every `count()` in that query then becomes `upsampled_count() as count` over non-error rows.

The gate also reads `request.GET["query"]` (line 135), not the `query` that `_get_event_stats` executes. In the dashboard split path, the third query is `({query}) AND event.type:transaction` (organization_events_stats.py:426-435). If the request query contains `event.type:error`, the transform is applied to that transactions-only query. Its result feeds `has_transactions`, which can change the split decision that `save_split_decision` persists (organization_events_stats.py:438).

The helper tests cover only the positive, `event.type:transaction`, and empty inputs, so none of this is caught. The fix is to decide from the query that will actually run and to parse the term instead of substring-matching it.

findings.title: Eligibility gate uses the outer `dataset`, not the dataset that runs the query
findings.description:
The gate passes the closure variable `dataset` set at line 170. `_get_event_stats` also receives `scoped_dataset`, and the split branches pass `discover` (lines 363, 370, 387). Split is entered only for metrics-enhanced datasets (line 344, with `metrics_enhanced` defined at line 191).

For a `metrics_enhanced_performance` widget, the error-only split query runs on `discover`, but the gate sees `metrics_enhanced_performance`. `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` then returns False (error_upsampling.py:126-127). The same error count is upsampled in plain discover and not upsampled through the dashboard split. The gate should use the dataset that actually executes.

findings.title: `sum(sample_weight)` assumes every row has a weight, but production sets it conditionally
findings.description:
The comments at discover.py:1044-1045 and error_upsampling.py:85-86 say the schema guarantees `sample_weight` for every event in allowlisted projects. Nothing in `src/` enforces that. `sample_weight` appears only in these two places. `event_manager.py:774-787` sets `sample_rate` only for allowlisted projects at ingest time, and only when `0 < rate <= 1`.

Events ingested before a project joined the allowlist, or without a valid rate, have no weight. If Snuba stores those as NULL or 0, the sum drops them, and enabling a project would make its historical counts fall. `toInt64` also truncates the float sum instead of rounding it. The Snuba default for a missing `sample_weight` is not in this repo, so I could not verify it. If it is NULL or 0, treat this as a FAIL. A possible fix is `ifNull(sample_weight, 1)`, with a test that includes an unweighted event.

findings.title: Upsampled `count` changes the response contract beyond the key name
findings.description:
With default flags the output key stays `count`, which matches the built-in alias, so the new tests pass. Three things still change:

- With `transformAliasToInputFormat=1`, the builder maps each alias back to `FunctionDetails.field` (`builder/base.py:1566-1572`). That field is the raw string, so the key becomes `upsampled_count() as count` instead of `count()`. `FunctionDetails.field` is `str` (`fields.py:2299-2300`).
- The result type changes from `integer` (`fields.py:1844`) to `number` (`discover.py:1051`).
- `upsampled_count` is registered as a public aggregate (`discover.py:1041`, no `private=True`) and is not documented.

The new endpoint tests assert only the default `count` key. Decide whether these changes are intended, and if not, keep the key and type stable.

findings.title: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is dead code, and its contract is not met
findings.description: Nothing in `src/` or `tests/` calls `invalidate_upsampling_cache`. Its docstring says it "should be called when the allowlist configuration changes", but nothing does that. The 60-second TTL (line 38) already bounds staleness. Its key is per exact project set, so clearing one set does not clear other queries that depend on the same allowlist entries. Remove it, or wire it up and test it.

findings.title: Docstrings and comments contradict the implementation
findings.description:
`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` says it "reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time" and calls that intentional. The public entry point caches the result for 60 seconds (lines 29-38), and the module docstring calls that cache "safe".

In the endpoint, the comments at organization_events_stats.py:218-219, 224-225 and 230-231 claim the early check "ensures consistent behavior", allows "better query optimization and caching", and "ensures we use the most current schema assumptions". None of that is true: the decision is not cached beyond the call, and the transform is repeated.

The performance reason for the cache is also weak. `src/sentry/options/store.py` already has a cache layer (`OptionsStore(cache=..., ttl=...)`, lines 68-83). Measure before keeping the extra 60-second cache, or remove it.

findings.title: Transform is repeated in three branches, and the decision is stored in two variables
findings.description:
The same `if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` appears at lines 232-233, 276-277 and 295-296. `upsampling_enabled` is just an alias of `should_upsample`. `final_columns = query_columns` is set before branches that always overwrite it.

Compute `final_columns` once, before `if top_events > 0:`, and use it at every call site. The result is the same, and it leaves one place to fix the gate, which is already wrong in two places.

findings.title: Tests mock the module's `options` instead of the repo's option override
findings.description: Four tests patch `sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options` (lines 3604, 3629, 3654, 3699). The existing event_manager tests use `with self.options({"issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist": [...]})` (tests/sentry/event_manager/test_event_manager.py:2881). A mock accepts any key and any value, so a misnamed option, a wrong type, or a registry change would not fail these tests.

findings.title: Test coverage misses the branches that carry the risk
findings.description:
Nothing covers:
- a negated query such as `!event.type:error`
- a dashboard split with an error-containing request query
- `topEvents`, since no integration test sends it, so the `top_events` branch at organization_events_stats.py:229-272 is untested
- the RPC branches
- SnQL resolution of `upsampled_count`
- events that lack a weight

`test_is_error_focused_query` covers only three inputs. Add tests for these cases before relying on the gate.

findings.title: Test factory swallows errors and diverges from ingest validation
findings.description:
The two bare `except Exception: pass` blocks hide failures. The first guards only against a non-dict `contexts` value, which a test fixture should not produce, so it hides a bad fixture instead of reporting it.

The docstring says "present and valid", but the helper validates nothing. It skips the `0 < rate <= 1` check that `event_manager.py:785-787` applies, and it ignores the allowlist gate at `event_manager.py:776`. It will happily set `2.0` or `float("nan")`, so tests can create events that production would never weight. Remove the try blocks, validate the same way ingest does, and let bad input fail loudly.

findings.title: Trailing whitespace on blank lines fails the repo's pre-commit hooks
findings.description: Blank lines with trailing spaces appear at error_upsampling.py lines 22, 28, 33, 36, 39, 49, 51 and 84, and at organization_events_stats.py lines 223, 234 and 278. `.pre-commit-config.yaml` runs `black` and a `trailing-whitespace` hook (line 179), so these fail the commit checks. Strip them.

findings.title: Unrelated `topEvents` message change
findings.description: The message changed from "If topEvents needs to be at least 1" to "topEvents needs to be at least 1". This now matches `organization_events_timeseries.py:134`, which is fine. The change is unrelated to upsampling, though, and it alters a user-visible error string. No test asserts the old text. Call it out in the PR description or split it into its own change.

findings.title: Cache key uses Python `hash()` of the project tuple
findings.description: `hash(tuple(sorted(...)))` produces a 64-bit integer, so two project sets can collide and return each other's cached eligibility for up to 60 seconds. The risk is small. Building the key from the sorted IDs (for example `",".join(map(str, ids))`) removes it, and the same change applies to `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (line 73).

findings.title: Inconsistent typing and split imports in the helper
findings.description: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` types `dataset` as `ModuleType` (line 16), but `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` takes `Any`. The `sentry.snuba` import is split across two local imports (lines 109 and 115). Use one type and one import. If the local import avoids a cycle, add a comment that says so.

findings.title: Test setup reassigns `self.user` after logging in
findings.description: `setUp` stores the logged-in user as `authed_user` (line 3560), then reassigns `self.user = self.create_user()` (line 3566). The events are tagged with the new user's email while the requests run as the original user. The tests pass as written, but the mismatch is easy to misread. Use a separate name for the event author.

findings.title: No injection, secret, or tenant-isolation problems in the new transform
findings.description: The query strings from `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` are fixed constants and are not built from user input. The cache key contains only the organization ID and project IDs, so it cannot leak across tenants. I found no security issues in the new code.
